content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels are ready‑to‑eat snack twists made from wheat flour, water, yeast and a pinch of salt. After baking they are brushed with melted butter and lightly sprinkled with sea salt, giving them a distinctive aroma and flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels have a medieval origin in Europe and were originally baked by monks.
The twisted shape is said to represent “interlaced arms,” a symbol of friendship and hospitality.
Soft pretzels are a classic accompaniment to beer in German and Austrian pubs.
Butter coating adds richness but also increases the calorie count.
In the 19th century they became a popular street food in the United States, especially in New York City.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pretzels provide a quick source of energy thanks to the complex carbs in the wheat dough.

items.title: Contains some protein
items.content: Wheat flour supplies a modest amount of plant‑based protein useful for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamin content
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough retains B1, B2 and niacin, which support metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Salt and a small amount of iron contribute to electrolyte balance.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: Butter and salt enhance flavor, helping to satisfy cravings and potentially reduce consumption of sweeter snacks.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Excessive intake of salted pretzels may contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Butter coating and carbs make the product energy‑dense; portion control is advisable.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Pretzels contain wheat, so they are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The butter topping can trigger reactions in individuals allergic to milk proteins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be enjoyed straight from the pack, warmed in a microwave or oven, and used as a base for sandwiches with cream cheese, hummus, or jam.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life store in the refrigerator to prevent drying out and butter spoilage.
